log.msg: WHY CLICKING A VIEW WORD WENT BLANK, and it was mine. `Router.go()` LOADS FIRST AND PUSHES THE URL SECOND — core/Router/Router.js says so in its own comment, "so a failed navigation leaves no history entry". So during a real in-app click, every page in the chain runs its `content()` while `location.pathname` is still the url being LEFT. The guard I added this morning to stop the board building itself twice reads `location.pathname !== page.url` and therefore skipped, and the reader got a page holding nothing but its own title. Reproduced exactly: land on /framework/ai/days/, click grid, and the active page is page--grid with zero visible boards and the literal text "grid". Every cold load passed, because a cold load already has the right url — which is precisely why it shipped. Fix: `defer_board()`, a setTimeout(...,0), which is the first moment the url is certainly final (go() resumes and calls pushState in a MICROtask, so a macrotask is guaranteed to be after it) — and unlike requestAnimationFrame a macrotask still runs in a hidden tab. Every board page also calls it from `activated()` now, so coming back to a view that was skipped once still draws. Proved: five clicks in a row (grid, timeline, days, grid, now) each keep exactly one visible board, zero console errors.

THE GUTTER, before -> after, measured against the rail's own right border at 1280 and 3440, and against the viewport's left edge at 400 (below 52em the rail is a top bar, so there is no rail border to measure from). The ONE offender was the grid view's "sorted by importance..." line: `.v3-sort` had `padding-block-end: 0.25em` and nothing else, and `.v3-wall` is `display: contents` so it cannot inset its children — the line sat at x=240.6, exactly 0.0px from the border, at every width. After: 15.1px at 1280, 14px at 400, 62.1px at 3440, the same gutter every card stands on. Every other view already had it: days/now/prompts 15.1 / 14 / 62.1 (their containers carry `padding: var(--pad)`), timeline's rail rows the same through `.v3-inbox`'s own pad.

THE GUTTER, the two things that are still not at the full --pad, both checked and both fine. (1) `.v3-axis-hour` and `.v3-axis-break` BOXES sit 2.1px from the border at 1280 and 39.3px at 3440 — they pull themselves out with a negative inline margin on purpose so the hour rule runs the column's full width, and they re-pad their own TEXT back to the gutter. That is paint bleeding, not text touching, which is the rule the layout skill already draws. (2) the usage footer's first text reads 13px at 1280 and 52px at 3440 rather than 15.1/62.1 — `--pad`'s floor is `1em` of the box it is in and that strip is typed at 0.8125rem, so its own one-em gutter is 13px. Left as it is: it is the strip's own scale, nothing is at 0, and forcing the page ramp onto a control strip is the exact mistake the css skill names.

THE GAP ABOVE THE CHROME LINE. `.v3-head` had `padding: var(--pad) var(--pad) 0`, and `--pad` is a PERCENTAGE of the containing block, so the space above the AI title measured 15.0px at 1280 but 62.1px at 3440 — a band of empty grey that grew with the screen, which is what the owner kept seeing. The block padding is now the row's own 0.6em: 9.0px at 1280, 8.4px at 400, 10.8px at 3440. The INLINE padding stays `var(--pad)`, because sideways this row has to stand on the same gutter as every card. Dead space above the first card, after this and the grid word going: 1280 202.4 -> 61.6, 400 373.4 -> 146.2, 1920 193.3 -> 69.7, 3440 97.6. Head height at 1280: 142.3 -> 46.6.

The alternative — dropping the negative margin — would have shortened the one rule that makes the timeline readable as a timeline, to satisfy a measurement of the wrong thing.

THE FIX THAT COVERS ALL OF THEM, and the microtask trap inside it. `watch_board()`: a page that was asked to draw while a deeper url was showing installs one MutationObserver on its own element, watching for the `.active-page` class the arrangement contract stamps on whatever is being shown — one observer, attributes only, disconnected the moment the board draws. First version read the old pathname on all three of the mutations it correctly observed, because a MutationObserver callback is a MICROtask and the class is stamped inside Router.activate(), before go() resumes and pushes the url — the same one tick early as the original bug. It goes through `defer_board()` (setTimeout 0) like everything else now. With the observer in place the five per-page `deactivated()` handoffs became redundant and were deleted: ai/page.js is 1,045 bytes shorter than when I added them, and there is one rule instead of one rule plus five hooks.

decision.topic: how a board page knows it is the one being shown
decision.say: it watches its own element for the .active-page class, rather than being told
decision.why: Three different navigations reach a board root, and only two of them can be intercepted from inside this fence: a click INTO it, a click back out of a view, and a click back up from a declared day page whose page.js belongs to somebody else. A per-child `deactivated()` handoff covers the first two and can never cover the third. The class the arrangement contract already stamps is the one signal all three share, it needs no cooperation from any child, and it let five hooks be deleted. Alternative considered: overriding `Page.child()` on this page to wrap every child's `deactivated` as it is created — same coverage, but it reaches into core's own method from a page config, which is a much bigger thing to own than one observer on one element.
